analysis.title: BP completes Castrol stake sale, ME diplomacy working? + Energy Daily 02/11/26
key_insights: Oil fell 3-3.5% on reports that Trump wants to give Iran diplomacy more time before any renewed strikes after Tuesday's US midterms. Brent dropped toward $110 and WTI was near $101. Part of the move reflects the front-month roll from Dec26 to Jan27 (Brent $109.5, WTI $100.5).

UBS specialist sales sees the midterms as more likely a catalyst for escalation than for diplomacy, whether Republicans beat expectations or Democrats surge. The desk expects the political risk premium, not Hormuz export volumes, to be the near-term focus even though the Hormuz tracker shows a bounce in oil and LNG exports.

Iranian negotiators held a third consecutive day of talks with Qatari mediators in Doha. Iran repeated its 2-day timeline for reopening the Strait of Hormuz if the US meets its demands, and said it would strike US and Israeli targets in the region if attacked again. Rubio said Trump has not decided on new strikes and prefers a diplomatic solution.

Friday was a heavy risk-off session (S&P 500 -1.8%, Nasdaq -2.9%) led by the AI trade. Semis, memory and neoclouds fell sharply, NVDA lost 4.2% and SPCX 6.4%. Treasury yields fell 2-8bps with the curve steepening, and the desk reports concern that the Treasury bid is starting to signal a growth scare.

Asia and US futures bounced Monday morning (ESA +40bps, NQA +80bps). Tokyo Electron rose 6.5% after earnings, but Kioxia fell 16% on a softer outlook. The desk says the AI complex likely needs more than one positive print out of Tokyo to signal the de-risking is over.

KOSPI rose 2% after reversing a 2% intraday low, helped by National Pension net buying of $190mn on top of Friday's $640mn, its largest single day of buying in nearly five years. China rose 1.1% through a soft PMI on reports that regulators will meet banks and brokers on capital market support.

Week ahead: ISM manufacturing and AAPL and PLTR earnings Monday, US midterms and RBA Tuesday, ISM services, Treasury refunding and QCOM Wednesday, BoE (25bp hike to 4% expected) Thursday, and October nonfarm payrolls Friday (65k expected vs 29k prior).
BP completed the sale of a 65% stake in Castrol to Stonepeak for $6bn of after-tax proceeds, to be used to reduce its financial obligations. BP keeps 35% and Castrol becomes a standalone company.

TotalEnergies is acquiring a 30% operated interest in the Lang Lebah and B14 gas fields off Sarawak, Malaysia, alongside PTTEP 25%, KUFPEC 25% and PCSB 20%. The fields hold over 6.5 tcf of gas resources and would feed the existing Malaysia LNG plant at a plateau of about 10 bcm per year. Financial terms were not disclosed.
Portugal's government will not rule out raising its 8% stake in Galp after talks with Spain's Moeve failed.

Venture Global's Plaquemines Phase 1 reached commercial operations, with Shell receiving the first long-term contract cargo. Contract pricing is to be significantly discounted from near 46-month highs of about $34/mmBtu at TTF and $32 at JKM.

OPEC+ kept December output targets unchanged. Seven core members made the decision, most Gulf members are still pumping well below targets, and the full group meets November 29 when analysts expect 2027 quotas to be set.

European gas storage is a stress point. German storage was 61.03% full on November 1 against an 80% target (GIE data show 61.17% against about 70%), with a cold snap setting in. Germany and Italy are disputing blame, and the US is pushing a plan to resume Russian pipeline gas to Europe via Ukraine through a US intermediary.

Freight rates for Russian oil to India are at records. Urals shipping costs are around $30/bbl or more, up from about $20 in September, which is eating into Russian sellers' profits. Russia plans 2.15 million tons of diesel exports in November and is preparing to extend its diesel export ban.

Chevron beat third-quarter adjusted profit expectations on higher refining margins, but guided Q4 upstream output down 175,000-225,000 boepd on turnarounds and downstream earnings down $400-500 million on maintenance. UBS flags the XOM Q3 beat with a higher dividend and lower leverage.
PTTEP shut in its Kikeh and SNP fields in Malaysia for FPSO restoration work, with resumption not expected until Q1 next year. Q3 average sales volumes fell 9% QoQ.

Petrobras refineries ran at 98% utilization in October and are expected to stay near the limit through December. YPF applied for Argentine incentives for its $8.73bn Bajo del Toro Vaca Muerta project. Imperial Oil is considering an earlier decision on its Aspen oil sands project.
CFTC data show speculators cut net long US crude positions by 6,616 contracts to 104,314 in the week to October 27.

UBS research: new BP price target of 725p and view that shares should slightly outperform, Repsol target raised slightly, Range Resources target raised to $54, GAIL estimates raised 15% on trading margins, and NTPC growth guidance cut on transmission delays. Valero is buying and restarting LYB's Houston refinery and HF Sinclair is buying 2.4M of its shares from REH for about $257M.

market_movers.rationale: UBS sets a new price target of 725p after the 3Q26 results and thinks the shares should slightly outperform ahead of the strategy update.
Repsol: UBS raises its price target slightly after the 3Q26 review, saying high margins and buybacks could support the shares near term.
UBS updates Range Resources estimates after 3Q26 earnings and lifts its price target to $54.
GAIL (India): UBS maintains Buy with an unchanged price target and raises FY27E earnings 15% on a strong EBITDA beat aided by gas trading.
NTPC: UBS maintains Buy despite cutting FY27 capacity addition to about 8GW on transmission delays.

earnings_insights: Chevron (reported 10/31): beat Wall Street expectations for Q3 adjusted profit as refining margins rose. Q4 guidance: upstream production down 175,000-225,000 boepd from turnarounds and downstream earnings down $400-500 million from planned maintenance.
ExxonMobil Q3 2026 (reported): UBS headline 'XOM Reports 3Q26 Beat, Higher Dividend and Lower Leverage', call takeaways cite strong upstream pricing and higher refining margins.
BP Q3 2026 (reported): UBS calls it a 'solid beat ahead of the strategy update' and sets a 725p price target.
GAIL Q2FY27 (reported): EBITDA +33% vs UBSe and +42% vs consensus. Gas trading EBIT Rs32.8bn vs UBSe Rs17.5bn, gas transmission EBIT Rs19.3bn (-4% vs UBSe).
Power Grid Corp of India Q2FY27 (reported): EBITDA Rs97bn (+7% YoY, in line with consensus), reported PAT Rs39bn (+8% YoY, +5% vs consensus).
Indraprastha Gas Q2FY27 (reported): EBITDA of negative Rs0.3bn on higher gas sourcing cost, volumes +8% YoY at 10.1mmscmd.
CNOOC Q3 2026 (reported): net profit dragged by falling oil prices and asset impairment losses, production stable QoQ. Sinopec H-share Q3 net profit rose 55% QoQ, beating UBS estimates.
PTTEP Q3 2026 (reported): average sales volumes 521,163 boepd vs 572,882 boepd in Q2 (-9%), average selling price $51.52/boe, slightly lower than Q2.

Upcoming earnings: AAPL and PLTR on Monday, QCOM on Wednesday. Other names above $100bn market cap reporting this week: AMD, AMGN, APO, ANET, ARM, BKNG, COIN, COP, DASH, DTE, EOG, ETN, F, FDX, ISRG, MCD, MELI, NVO, PFE, SHOP, SONY, TTE, UBER, VRTX.

macro_indicators.interpretation: Brent fell on reports Trump will give Iran diplomacy more time, after rising more than 2% on Friday. The Dec to Jan front-month roll explains part of the drop.
WTI moved in line with Brent on the diplomacy headlines and the contract roll.
Friday's October jobs report is the key data point of the week, after a Treasury bid that some read as a growth scare.
Thursday's BoE decision is a key central bank event alongside Norges Bank and ECB speakers.

macro_indicators.reading: 61.03% full (INES, Nov 1) vs 80% target, and 61.17% (GIE, Friday) vs about 70% goal
macro_indicators.interpretation: Record low storage ahead of winter with a cold snap in progress adds to European gas supply concerns.
Peak demand in October was 260.7GW (+23.7% YoY), well above prior months' growth of 10.9% in September and 12.1% in August.

macro_indicators.indicator: CFTC speculator net long, US crude
macro_indicators.interpretation: Speculators reduced net long exposure to crude ahead of the diplomacy headlines.
Russia plans to extend its diesel export ban while allowing quota exports to meet a new commitment to the US.

risk_factors: US midterms on Tuesday could trigger Iran escalation rather than de-escalation, according to the UBS specialist sales desk.
Renewed US strikes on Iran and Iranian retaliation against US and Israeli targets in the region.
AI trade de-risking could continue if Tokyo earnings do not deliver more than one positive print, with the high guidance bar shown by Kioxia's 16% drop.
A Treasury bid that signals a growth scare rather than a pure safe-haven move.
European gas shortage this winter, with record low German storage and a cold snap under way.
Disruption to LNG and oil shipping near the Strait of Hormuz.
vol_and_positioning: Friday US equity flow was balanced (48/52) with participation about 20% below the YTD average. Banks (25% of turnover) were the busiest sector, with demand in Spanish and Dutch names. Healthcare saw demand in large-cap pharma, Technology saw supply in software, and Energy saw supply.
Speculators cut combined US crude net longs by 6,616 contracts to 104,314 in the week to October 27 (CFTC).
National Pension Service bought a net $190mn of Korean equities Monday after $640mn Friday, its largest single day in nearly five years.
geopolitical: Iran-US talks via Qatari mediators in Doha entered a third day, with Iran repeating a 2-day timeline to reopen the Strait of Hormuz if the US meets its demands.
Trump reportedly told Netanyahu he prefers diplomacy, which concerned the Israeli prime minister (Axios). WSJ and NYT reporting suggests Trump is also preparing military options again.
US midterm elections on Tuesday, with polls pointing to a Democratic surge. The UBS desk sees the midterms as a possible catalyst for escalation.
A Pakistan-bound LNG carrier, Al Mayeda, was attacked near Hormuz on Friday after Iran had reportedly approved its passage.
US officials are promoting resumed Russian gas sales to Europe via Ukraine through a US intermediary, as part of talks on an energy ceasefire before winter.
Germany and Italy are in a public dispute over German gas storage filling, which Germany calls 'unfounded' blame.
Trump said the US has the 'concept' of a trade deal with Canada, and Canada and the EU are exploring more Canadian LNG exports to Europe.
Black Sea risks and a tanker shortage keep Russian crude freight rates at records.
